# Benchmark report

## What was measured, and how

Every number in this report was read from a result file under runs/, written by the benchmark suite in this repository at the commit named below. Each scenario ran in fresh processes, and the samples of all its processes were pooled. Timings are reported as nearest-rank percentiles (p50, p95, p99) with a bootstrap interval of the percentile (1,000 resamples, seed 4747); no mean and no best run is reported.

A budget is met only when the whole interval lies at or under it, and missed only when the whole interval lies over it; an interval that crosses a limit is undecided. A percentile is decided only over enough samples: 10 for p50, 40 for p95 and 200 for p99, and for keystrokes and frames at least 200 kept in each process, after the first tenth of each process's samples (at least 20) is dropped as warm-up. A timing budget needs at least five processes. A figure with one value per process, a size and a count are compared directly with their limit. A budget is judged only on the tier named for it, at 1x and outside a quick run; every other run is reported and not judged.

Before each scenario the runner checked that the machine was quiet: a one-minute load average at or under a quarter of the cores it sees (at least 1), and a fixed calibration loop whose 90th-percentile time was at most 1.25 times its 10th. It checked every 5 seconds for up to one minute; a scenario that never found the machine quiet is reported as void, with what the check saw.

No proof run was published.

To run one row again, check out the commit, run bun install --frozen-lockfile, then bun run bench fetch-traces (for the editing traces) and bun run bench --tier <tier> --filter <scenario>. Docker must be running for every tier but host; the tiers are containers with the limits in the table above, built from the two base images named above.

## Limits of the method

1. A container's processor limit gives a fast core in bursts, not a slow core, so typing is also measured with Chromium's processor slowdown at 4 and 6 times.
2. The slowdown stretches the page's own JavaScript, style and layout on its main thread. It does not slow the browser's other processes, the network, the disk, memory bandwidth, the server or the sync path, and it does not model a slower graphics card or a hot laptop that lowers its clock. A 4x figure is a bound for script cost on a slower processor, not a prediction for any one laptop.
3. Containers have no graphics card, so paint times read worse than on a real machine.
4. Docker runs Linux only. Windows is checked on shared CI machines for whether the app works, never for timing; macOS is measured directly on one Apple-silicon laptop, the host tier. Processor emulation is never used for timing.
5. Server figures come from the D-small container, where the simulated clients share the server's one core, so they read worse than a server alone would.
6. Headless browsers have no spellchecker, so spellcheck is measured in headed Chromium with a virtual display.
7. Simulated: writers and readers at the rates of the profiles above, generated scripts and prose, and offline hours compressed into seconds. Not simulated: real typists, real networks with loss and delay, and browsers other than Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
8. The power-loss model copies files while writing and models a cut that keeps what reached the file system, not the disk's cache.

## Limits to state first

1. The 2,000-page length is a target, not a promise. The measured comfort limit of each tier stands in its place: D-modest 300 pages, D-modest 4x 30 pages, D-typical none, host 2,000 pages.
2. A project can hold thousands of documents and any number of versions, because neither is loaded with the script being edited.
3. Offline storage in a browser is kept at the browser's discretion; the desktop app is the durable offline client.
4. Who wrote each character is kept character by character only since the newest checkpoint; older versions record it per block.
5. Characters outside the script font are kept, but not typeset or printed correctly.
6. The half of the wrong design that keeps thousands of versions inside the live document cannot be built here, so it is not measured and no figure is given.

## Comfort envelope

| Scenario         | D-modest                          | D-modest 4x                       | D-typical    | host                            |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------- |
| typing-30        | 12.0 ms (11.5–12.6) comfortable   | 20.1 ms (19.0–21.5) comfortable   | not measured | 4.0 ms (3.8–4.3) comfortable    |
| typing-120       | 14.2 ms (13.8–14.9) comfortable   | 38.0 ms (35.1–41.2) usable        | not measured | 5.5 ms (5.2–5.9) comfortable    |
| typing-300       | 28.4 ms (27.1–29.9) comfortable   | 55.0 ms (51.0–60.0) uncomfortable | not measured | 7.0 ms (6.6–7.5) comfortable    |
| typing-1000      | 41.0 ms (36.2–45.8) usable        | 80.0 ms (62.0–99.0) undecided     | not measured | 12.0 ms (11.2–12.9) comfortable |
| typing-2000      | 62.0 ms (55.0–70.4) uncomfortable | not measured                      | not measured | 19.0 ms (18.1–20.2) comfortable |
| typing-book-1000 | 18.0 ms (17.2–19.1) comfortable   | not measured                      | not measured | not measured                    |
| typing-book-2000 | 21.5 ms (20.4–22.9) comfortable   | not measured                      | not measured | not measured                    |

D-modest: comfortable to 300 pages (7,500 blocks); usable to 1,000 pages (25,000 blocks).

D-modest 4x: comfortable to 30 pages (750 blocks); usable to 120 pages (3,000 blocks).

D-typical: comfortable at no measured length; usable at no measured length.

host: comfortable to 2,000 pages (50,000 blocks); usable to 2,000 pages (50,000 blocks).

## Past the comfortable length

The app shows one notice, on every device, once a script passes 300 pages: '&lt;title&gt;' is longer than this device handles comfortably, so typing may slow down. That figure comes from one reference machine. The measured comfort limits are: D-modest 300 pages, D-modest 4x 30 pages, D-typical none, host 2,000 pages. A slower device slows down before it is told; a faster one is told early.

## Where it breaks

| Mechanism                                     | Cause                                                                                   | Solution adopted                                                                                               | Rows                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The editable page grows with the script       | Every block is an element the browser keeps and lays out                                | The script is split into sections of about 100 blocks, and the browser skips the layout of sections off screen | typing-30, typing-120, typing-300, typing-1000, typing-2000, typing-book-1000, typing-book-2000, typing-flat-1000, open-120 |
| Remote changes cost the whole document        | Each remote change replaces the editor's whole document                                 | Remote changes are merged into one update per frame                                                            | typing-120 remote_extra                                                                                                     |
| Writer identities pile up with sessions       | Each editing session adds a writer identity to the document, and the list never shrinks | The document is rebuilt once it passes a size or identity budget                                               | not measured                                                                                                                |
| History inside the live document              | Every kept version would make the live document larger                                  | Versions are kept outside the live document                                                                    | not measured                                                                                                                |
| A join storm encodes the room for each client | Each joining client asks for the whole state                                            | The state is encoded once for all the clients that join together                                               | not measured                                                                                                                |
| Long jobs on the serving thread               | A long job on the thread that serves sockets delays every room                          | Checkpoints are written by a worker; rebuilds and replays still run on the serving thread                      | not measured                                                                                                                |
| Slow readers                                  | A client that does not read its socket makes the server buffer without limit            | The server closes a connection whose send buffer passes a limit                                                | server.fanout                                                                                                               |
| A daily document reused for weeks             | Deleting yesterday's text keeps its history inside the document                         | A new document each day                                                                                        | crdt.daily-reuse                                                                                                            |

## The wrong design, on purpose

This section measures a layout the app does not use, to show what it avoids: one 1,000-page script in a single section beside the same length in sections, and one daily document reused for 60 days beside a new document each day. The single-section script is measured with one typist, not ten writers and fifty readers. Its second half, a document that keeps 3,000 versions inside itself, cannot be built, because the CRDT layer has no switch that keeps deleted history; it is not measured, and no figure is given.

| Scenario         | D-modest            | D-modest 4x         | D-typical    | host                |
| ---------------- | ------------------- | ------------------- | ------------ | ------------------- |
| typing-flat-1000 | 180 ms (170–195)    | not measured        | not measured | not measured        |
| typing-1000      | 41.0 ms (36.2–45.8) | 80.0 ms (62.0–99.0) | not measured | 12.0 ms (11.2–12.9) |

| Scenario                            | D-modest | D-typical    |
| ----------------------------------- | -------- | ------------ |
| crdt.daily-reuse bytes_ratio_reused | 41.7     | not measured |
| crdt.daily-reuse bytes_ratio_fresh  | 2.3      | not measured |

## The long book

The long book is generated prose in the manuscript format, at 1,000 and 2,000 pages, typed beside screenplays of the same lengths. A page of prose holds far fewer blocks than a page of a script, so the comparison shows whether cost follows blocks or words. It is measured with one typist, not two writers and five readers, and without its 200 versions.

| Scenario         | Blocks | Characters   | D-modest            | D-modest 4x         | D-typical    | host                |
| ---------------- | ------ | ------------ | ------------------- | ------------------- | ------------ | ------------------- |
| typing-book-1000 | 4,100  | not measured | 18.0 ms (17.2–19.1) | not measured        | not measured | not measured        |
| typing-1000      | 25,000 | not measured | 41.0 ms (36.2–45.8) | 80.0 ms (62.0–99.0) | not measured | 12.0 ms (11.2–12.9) |
| typing-book-2000 | 8,200  | not measured | 21.5 ms (20.4–22.9) | not measured        | not measured | not measured        |
| typing-2000      | 50,000 | not measured | 62.0 ms (55.0–70.4) | not measured        | not measured | 19.0 ms (18.1–20.2) |

## Trade-offs

| #   | Trade-off                                                                                | What we gain                                                                                                        | What we give up, and where the limit is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Rows that bear on it                                                                                |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | CRDT instead of a central authority                                                      | Offline edits of any age merge without dropping steps                                                               | For an online-only product an authority model is simpler and would be the better pick. A CRDT server cannot cheaply tell what an accepted update _means_: scene assignment, who may accept a suggestion and the ban on suggesting after lock are enforced in the interface only. Everything that must be exact — versions, locks, issues, numbers — is therefore sequenced by the cloud, not merged                                                               | not measured                                                                                        |
| 2   | Rebuilding a document when it is over budget                                             | Typing cost and size stay flat however long a show runs                                                             | Every rebuild turns later offline arrivals from a character-level merge into a block-level replay and resets undo. After 90 days an arrival is a side-by-side manual merge, which is the kind of recovery we criticise in others. So rebuilds are rare, never scheduled, and never inside an air window                                                                                                                                                           | not measured                                                                                        |
| 3   | Invisible sections with `content-visibility`                                             | A keystroke at 1,000 pages cost 1.4 ms instead of 17.8 ms in a bare-ProseMirror spike                               | More editor complexity at every section boundary, and a browser feature with a recorded caret bug in editable content. Nothing is measured at 2,000 pages, with the real engine, or with Yjs attached. The fallback costs about five times more per keystroke and brings a lower, measured comfort limit                                                                                                                                                          | typing-30, typing-120, typing-300, typing-1000, typing-2000, typing-flat-1000, the comfort envelope |
| 4   | Arithmetic pagination                                                                    | Every collaborator and the PDF agree on every page, with no measuring and no feedback loop                          | No page-for-page parity with other screenwriting tools, whose Courier faces are not exactly 10 characters per inch. Parity is promised only for characters in the script font; wide, right-to-left and complex scripts are kept but not typeset or printed correctly. On Firefox and Safari wrap mismatches are tracked and corrected on screen, not blocked                                                                                                      | no measurement bears on this                                                                        |
| 5   | History outside the live document                                                        | The live document stays small no matter how many versions and revisions exist                                       | Authorship is per character only in the log since the newest checkpoint; before that, and once a log is dropped, it is per block, per version. History between two syncs is the device's snapshots (at most hourly), not keystroke by keystroke as the device saw it                                                                                                                                                                                              | not measured                                                                                        |
| 6   | Browser storage for offline work on the web                                              | The web app works offline with nothing installed                                                                    | A browser can clear it; Safari does so after a period without use. A script that exists "only in this browser" says so. Persistent storage is requested on the first change of a session, except in Firefox, where the request asks the person a question and is made only from Preferences. When a browser clears everything, its device identity goes too, so what existed only there cannot be named afterwards. The desktop app is the durable offline client | no measurement bears on this                                                                        |
| 7   | One server process                                                                       | One thing to deploy, back up and reason about; exact ordering for free                                              | A crash or a deploy stops sync and prompter updates for every project until it restarts, and making versions and issuing run on the same machine as serving (trade-off 20). Clients keep working offline through it. More than one writer host needs the Postgres driver                                                                                                                                                                                          | server.fanout                                                                                       |
| 8   | Electrobun                                                                               | The desktop app's main process is Bun; one runtime                                                                  | A young project with a small team behind it, three months into 2.0; file associations on macOS only; unmeasured with bundled Chromium. Builds are unsigned, so users see a warning at first open, and updates come from public releases                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | no measurement bears on this                                                                        |
| 9   | Installer size                                                                           | A self-contained app with identical rendering on three systems                                                      | The compiled server alone is 85–110 MB per target; the desktop app adds Chromium on top. The benchmark reports the real installer size against a budget                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | the desktop installer size                                                                          |
| 10  | Full scope in one release                                                                | Nothing the owner asked for is designed out                                                                         | Risk concentrates. The build order puts the core first and every step ships only with its tests; what is finished runs and can be shown, and the stages after the core — working with other people, variety and news, admin and the remaining formats — follow in that order. The report says which stages were reached                                                                                                                                           | no measurement bears on this                                                                        |
| 11  | Derived revision marks                                                                   | No stale marks; identical on every client                                                                           | A retyped or copied block has a new ID and is marked whole                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | no measurement bears on this                                                                        |
| 12  | One Writing switch, comments in rounds, History as a tab, one Send screen                | Fewer things to learn: five kinds of surface and one word per thing                                                 | A private draft and formal feedback are not things of their own in the interface. An executive's note looks like any comment until the round's name is read. An old version is shown in the page's place, so the state bar's sentence must be unmistakable. Issue looks less special than it did                                                                                                                                                                  | no measurement bears on this                                                                        |
| 13  | Nine preferences, no key sets, no preferences file                                       | Defaults carry almost everyone, and nothing personal can move a page                                                | No second page font and no in-app reduce-motion. Theme cannot differ per device except through System. A writer cannot adopt another tool's keys in one step. Two changes to one preference are ordered by device clocks, and a reset is final after 30 seconds                                                                                                                                                                                                   | no measurement bears on this                                                                        |
| 14  | A dark sheet in the dark theme; the band in place of the tint; stock components unedited | Less light at night; a revision can be told in both themes; one class list per component                            | A dark sheet has less contrast headroom than white paper (the worst stacked case is 4.59:1 against 4.71:1). A paper's colour shows on 8 px, not the whole page, unless the tint is switched on. `dark:` classes cannot be used at all. There is one density. High contrast cannot be tried on part of a screen                                                                                                                                                    | no measurement bears on this                                                                        |
| 15  | Healing a restored server from clients, bounded by what it had acknowledged              | A restored backup loses nothing a client still holds, and no client can inject another person's unacknowledged text | Text beyond the restored acknowledgement record comes back as the edits of whoever held it, so after a restore some words can carry the wrong author                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | no measurement bears on this                                                                        |
| 16  | Sections never move an existing block                                                    | A merge can never lose an edit to a container move                                                                  | Dual dialogue that straddles a section boundary is drawn stacked on screen while the PDF keeps the columns; on that page the screen differs from the PDF. A rebuild keeps every dual run inside one section                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | no measurement bears on this                                                                        |
| 17  | Removed text drawn on the page in Changes since                                          | A writer reads what went where it was                                                                               | While changes are shown on the page, lines carrying removed text run past the engine's page and are not corrected; Side by side and As it was keep exact pages                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | no measurement bears on this                                                                        |
| 18  | Overlap detection while online                                                           | Two people changing one speech within 3 seconds are both told                                                       | It is approximate: "theirs" is the block without this device's recent typing, so a deletion this device made of the other person's text in that window cannot be undone from the review                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | no measurement bears on this                                                                        |
| 19  | The log is kept until a rebuild                                                          | Every acknowledged edit stays in an append-only, checksummed log: exact versions and recovery                       | Storage grows with every keystroke, about 0.8 MB per typist-hour, until a rebuild replaces it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | not measured                                                                                        |
| 20  | Heavy work on the serving thread                                                         | One process, no worker protocol for the rarer jobs                                                                  | A rebuild of a 2,000-page script, a replay whose base is rebuilt from a long log, making a version of a long script, and drawing an issued PDF run inline and can stall other documents; each moves to the checkpoint worker if the benchmark shows a stall over 20 ms                                                                                                                                                                                            | not measured                                                                                        |
| 21  | Two durable writes per keystroke on desktop                                              | "Saved" means the device's own store, whatever the cloud does                                                       | Every keystroke is written twice, to the node's log and to the upstream outbox, on the same disk; a setting change is acknowledged before the upstream outbox holds it, so a crash in that gap can lose a setting change, never text                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | desktop.saved-fsync                                                                                 |
| 22  | Cursors sent as block and offset with a position hint                                    | No CRDT internals in presence; cursors survive a rebuild                                                            | A cursor whose block is more than 200 blocks from its hint is hidden until it moves                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | not measured                                                                                        |
| 23  | A revision's date from the issuing device                                                | A server in another time zone cannot change a header                                                                | A device with a wrong calendar stamps a wrong date                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | no measurement bears on this                                                                        |
| 24  | Seeding the demo through the real write path                                             | The demo's history, versions and revisions are what the product would have made                                     | The large workspace takes minutes to seed, in the background                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | demo.seed                                                                                           |
| 25  | One comfort limit for every device                                                       | A notice that is honest about long scripts from the first release                                                   | The figure is measured on one reference machine; a slower device slows down before it is told, a faster one is told early                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | the comfort envelope                                                                                |
| 26  | Cursor colours given by the server, in the order people first open a script for editing  | The first ten people on a script never share a colour, and a colour never changes                                   | Someone who opened the script for editing and never typed still holds a colour; the eleventh person shares the first one's colour and is told apart by the name tab                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | no measurement bears on this                                                                        |
| 27  | The PDF is written in the page, from the pagination already on screen                    | Export and Print work offline, with no server, and the file's pages are the screen's                                | Writing a very long script's PDF occupies the window while the Send screen shows its busy state; at 2,000 pages that can take seconds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | not measured                                                                                        |
| 28  | An issued revision's file is drawn again from what was issued each time it is asked for  | Nothing extra is stored, and the file always matches the issued version                                             | Its pages, lines and marks never change; its bytes may differ between releases of the PDF library, because they are not stored                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | no measurement bears on this                                                                        |

## Other designs and other figures

These figures have no budget. They are measured so that the choices this app made can be weighed against the alternatives, and so that features without a stated target have a figure.

On the editing traces, Yjs (this app) is measured beside prosemirror-collab (central-authority baseline), Loro and Automerge.

## Not measured

- export.pdf-120 on D-typical: could not finish: export.pdf-120 pdf_ms was budgeted and not measured.
- crdt.traces on D-typical: the editing traces are not fetched: run bun run bench fetch-traces.
- typing-120 on D-typical: the machine was not quiet: load 3.4, calibration spread 1.6.
- server.fanout on D-small: Docker is not running, so the Docker tiers are recorded as not measured. Start Docker and run bun run bench again to measure them.
- server.join-storm on D-small: Docker is not running, so the Docker tiers are recorded as not measured. Start Docker and run bun run bench again to measure them.
- Typing with remote editors — Extra p95 over solo: no run holds crowd-120.
- Saving — Keystroke to "Saved" p95, web / desktop with full fsync: no run holds saved-web-120.
- Pagination — Engine work per keystroke: no run holds pagination-engine-400, pagination-engine-2000.
- Pagination — Full cold repagination, 120 / 400 / 2,000 pages: no run holds pagination-engine-400, pagination-engine-2000.
- Pagination — Frame in which many breaks move: no run holds repaginate-120, repaginate-2000.
- Paste 50 pages — To next paint: no run holds paste-50.
- Scroll — Frame time p95; frames over 50 ms: no run holds scroll-120, scroll-2000.
- Convergence — Update visible elsewhere, p50 / p99: no run holds convergence-120.
- Convergence — Prompter-feed staleness p99: no run holds prompter.staleness.
- Offline merge — Time to converge; longest task: no run holds merge-offline-120, merge-offline-book-2000, crdt.rebuild-time.
- Versions — List of 5,000 interactive; changes between two 120-page versions; restore: no run holds history.list.first_page, history.compare.120, history.restore.120, rundown.w4.
- Versions — At 2,000 pages: changes between two versions (no slice over 16 ms); making a version on the serving thread; restore: no run holds history.compare.2000, history.version.2000, history.restore.2000.
- Export — PDF, 120 pages: no run on D-modest judged export.pdf-120 pdf_ms.
- Client memory — Heap for a 120-page / 2,000-page script; growth over a 2-hour soak: no run holds open-2000, soak-client-120.
- Document size — Live bytes ÷ plain text; client IDs: no run holds crdt.rebuild-size, crdt.aged.
- Server — Fan-out p99 at 200 clients; event-loop lag p99: no run holds rundown.w4, rundown.w5.
- Server — Memory per idle room; per loaded 120-page room: no run holds server.room-memory, rundown.w5.
- Server — Join storm, 200 clients, last synced: no run holds rundown.w5.
- Storage — Growth per typist-hour (14,400 single-keystroke pushes; the log is kept until a rebuild); checkpoint stall on the serving thread: no run holds server.persistence.
- Storage — Serving-thread stall of one rebuild of a 2,000-page script, and of a replay whose base is built from a long log (p99): no run holds server.rebuild-stall.
- Durability — Acknowledged updates lost across 200 kills: no run holds server.durability.
- Desktop — Cold start, launch to the first frame; idle memory of all the app's processes, 30 s after the first frame: the desktop smoke results of the three systems were not available to this run.
- Interface — Interaction to next paint outside the page: no run holds interface-2000.
- Interface — Open a menu, popover or the palette: no run holds interface.
- Interface — Open or close a loaded panel; open a dialog: no run holds interface.
- Interface — Change screen (frame painted); open Preferences: no run holds interface.
- Interface — A preference or setting takes effect (attribute; theme at 2,000 pages): no run holds interface, interface-2000.
- Interface — Switch person: no run holds interface.
- Interface — Start-up: the static frame replaced by the real one: no run holds interface.
- Interface — Entry chunk; any other interface chunk except data and editor (gzip): no check measures the size of the web app's code in this release.
- Interface — Facts and outline published per keystroke; the palette's search: no run holds interface.
- Server — One keystroke through the write path, 120 / 2,000 pages: no run holds server.push-cost.
- Server — Memory growth over the 8-hour soak; every bot holding the same text at its end: no run holds server.soak.
- Production — Revision marks per keystroke, 120 pages with 12 revisions: no run holds production.marks.
- Durability — Acknowledged updates lost across simulated power cuts: no run holds server.power-loss.
- The log of 900,000 updates behind a W1 typing run: typing reads only the live document, and the log lies outside it; the log's growth is measured by `server.persistence`.
- The other writers and readers of W6 and W7, and W7's 200 versions: each is measured with one typist and no versions.
- The 24-hour soak: it is run by hand, not in a published run.
- Real modest hardware: no modest machine was available; the D-modest container stands in for one.
- Rollback: the app has no rollback step to time in this release.
- Aged-document workloads for Loro and Automerge: only the editing traces are replayed into Loro and Automerge in this release.
